svg.title: a11y-loop, an open-source Agent Skill and command-line tool by Chan Meng. The skill gives a coding agent its accessibility rules while it writes UI. The CLI then audits the rendered page in a real browser across five passes (default, dark, forced-colors, reduced-motion, reflow), the agent fixes what was found, and the audit runs again until the report converges. On the demo page, 163 seeded failures went to 0 and diff reported none introduced. The clean run still listed 15 manual checks automation cannot judge, such as testing with a real screen reader. In a small benchmark of 6 components, one run each and self-audited, violations went from 35 with no guidance to 1 with the skill and 0 after the loop: an illustration, not a study. Only 17 of the 55 WCAG 2.2 A and AA criteria have any automated rule, so a clean report is not a conformance claim. Built for the accessible-UI challenge set at the Aotearoa AI Hackathon 2026. MIT licence.
